summary: solana-py-utils ships install-time credential and wallet stealer exfiltrating to ntfy.sh
details: The sdist's setup.py unconditionally runs the bundled hxboot.py via subprocess under the current Python interpreter during pip install. hxboot.py reads installer-owned secrets including ~/.aws/credentials, ~/.ssh/id_* keys, ~/.netrc, ~/.pypirc, ~/.npmrc, kube/docker/gh/gcloud configuration, Solana keypair files (~/.config/solana/id.json, wallet.json),.env files, and *.pem/*.key material, and scrapes environment variables matching KEY/SECRET/TOKEN/PASS/MNEM/SEED/PRIV/API/WALLET. It additionally enumerates Chromium/Chrome/Brave/Edge user profiles for the MetaMask (nkbihfbeogaeaoehlefnkodbefgpgknn), Phantom (bfnaelmomeimhlpmgjnjophhpkkoljpa), and another wallet extension (bhhhlbepdkbapadjdnnojkbgioiodbic) Local Extension Settings, and base64-encodes the leveldb.log/.ldb contents. The aggregated data is POSTed via urllib to the hardcoded topic https://ntfy.sh/hx83e33eb9. The package name mimics legitimate Solana tooling (typosquat of solana-py), and the stealer fires automatically on `pip install` on every platform that builds the sdist.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
